After several consecutive weeks of ChatGPT users being limited only by weekly usage caps, OpenAI announced today that it will restore the five-hour usage limits for Codex and ChatGPT Work for Plus subscribers. Details below.

ChatGPT Plus subscribers see five-hour usage cap restored

OpenAI's Head of Codex and ChatGPT Engineering Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux announced tonight that, starting tomorrow (the 25th), the five-hour usage limits for Codex and ChatGPT Work will be restored for Plus subscribers.

When users hit either the five-hour or weekly usage cap, they can either wait for the next cycle to reset their usage, or purchase additional credits. OpenAI will also periodically reset usage caps for free, and stored reset credits can be earned through designated promotional campaigns and referral offers.

However, over the past few weeks, OpenAI temporarily lifted the five-hour usage limits for Codex and ChatGPT Work, keeping only the weekly usage cap in place.

During this period, the company also reset users' weekly usage early on several occasions to celebrate milestones, including reaching a combined one million active users across the two (now unified) platforms.

However, as Tibo explained tonight on X:

"We will fully restore the five-hour usage limit for Plus accounts on ChatGPT Work and Codex tomorrow. I mentioned this before but postponed it. This is necessary because (1) the five-hour limit helps us balance compute load, enabling us to maintain a generous weekly allowance, and (2) most Plus users are casual and new users who tend to accidentally burn through an entire week's quota and feel confused, leading to a poor experience. Over the coming months, the Pro $100 and Pro $200 subscriptions will continue not to have the five-hour limit enforced."

Tibo did not mention any changes for Enterprise or Edu accounts, which currently run on a separate credit-based usage system.

Does the restoration of the five-hour limit on ChatGPT Work and Codex affect you? Let us know in the comments.
